title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for polyneuropathy and diabetes.

HPI
The patient is a 62-year-old male presenting for a routine follow-up of type 2 diabetes and associated peripheral neuropathy. The patient reports mild tingling and occasional numbness in both feet. He notes that his blood glucose levels have remained stable. He continues to manage his glucose levels through diet and exercise alone. He denies any acute worsening of symptoms or new episodes of paresthesia.

Medication List
Multivitamin daily.

Exam
The patient is alert and oriented. Physical exam reveals intact sensation to light touch in the upper extremities. There is diminished sensation to monofilament testing in the bilateral great toes and first metatarsal heads. No active ulcers or skin breakdown noted.

Assessment
1. Type 2 diabetes mellitus: Currently diet controlled with no pharmacological interventions.
2. Polyneuropathy: The patient exhibits clinical signs of peripheral neuropathy. It is noted that this condition is unrelated to diabetes.

Plan
Continue current lifestyle modifications. Monitor foot health monthly. Follow up in three months for continued management.
explanations: The provider states the polyneuropathy is not diabetic: code diabetes without complications and the polyneuropathy separately.
Polyneuropathy not due to diabetes is coded separately (G62.9 when no cause is specified).

distractors.why: Documentation of another cause overrides the 'with' presumption.
The polyneuropathy still needs its own code.
